Subject: Post-demo follow-up: SDK auth, routing, and req/resp tokenization

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today. Good alignment on high-level goals: low-latency chat for customer support workflows, reranker for search relevance, and embedding-based semantic search for knowledge base retrieval. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of ask from Ignite:
- Embed + reranker pipeline for KB (40M docs approximate).
- Chat endpoint for live support with <200ms p50 latency target per request.
- Ability to call external tools (ticketing, calendar) from model responses.

Key technical topics to resolve (we covered these at a high level; want to confirm details):
1) SDK & auth: you’ll use server-side API keys with per-route scoping. For client SDKs we recommend short-lived tokens via your backend (we included sample code).
2) Routing/fallback: plan to route production traffic to a Quantized Llama-variant for cost, with automatic fallback to a higher-accuracy variant on error/timeout.
3) Structured output / tool calling: use our function-calling style JSON envelope. We’ll share a schema for the ticketing tool and an example of extracting structured actions.
4) Req/resp schema questions: choice between chat vs completions for your use case (we recommend chat for tool-calling and structured responses). Also need to agree on tokenization, max_tokens, stop behavior and streaming semantics for partial results to meet latency SLOs.

Next steps I can own this week:
- Share a concise integration notes doc with SDK snippets and an auth exchange example (attached).
- Sketch a routing policy example (canary to quantized model, auto-fallback to higher-cost model).
- Provide an embeddings + reranker throughput estimate based on your doc count and update cadence.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the auth/token exchange and whether you prefer an SDK-first or API-only approach for the PoC?

Thanks,
Ben

--

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our end: 

1) Auth ownership: Priya (cc) will own the backend integration. We currently use short-lived JWTs issued by our auth service, so if you can show the exchange pattern (backend redeems long-lived key for short token scoped to model/route) that would be ideal.

2) SDK vs API: We prefer SDK-first for the PoC to speed onboarding — Node + Python.

3) Embeddings scale: 40M docs is an estimate. We’ll be batching ingestion and updating embeddings nightly; throughput during initial sync is important but not latency-critical. For reranker, we plan to run a rerank on top-50 candidates from the embedding index. Any guidance on per-request tokenization for the reranker (how to set max_tokens, stop sequences) would help.

4) Streaming for chat: we like streaming partial tokens to show progressive UI, but we need to understand how streaming interacts with function/tool calls (if the model decides to call a tool mid-stream). Would streaming be cut when a tool call payload is emitted, or does the SDK buffer?

Also looping in our infra lead (cc) — we’ll want a short tech-only call this week to walk the team through the auth snippet and routing policy.

—Samir

Samir — great questions. Quick answers inline and a couple of concrete snippets in the attached files. I’ll also schedule a 30-min tech sync once you confirm windows.

Inline:
1) Auth exchange: recommended pattern (attached: redwood-auth-snippet.py) — your backend calls our token service with your long-lived service key to mint a short-lived token scoped to the routes/models you need. On the client, your UI requests a token from your backend which then uses it to call Redwood’s SDK. This avoids embedding secrets in the client.

2) SDK-first: we’ll provide both Node and Python examples. SDKs support automatic reconnects on transient errors and will surface streaming events to your UI via an event emitter.

3) Reranker tokenization / max_tokens: for reranking top-50 candidates we recommend using our completion-style reranker API with a small context window. Practical defaults: max_tokens: 128 for candidate scoring, stop: ["\n\n--END--"] if you use explicit markers. If you run into truncated prompts due to token limits, we use our tokenizer probe in the SDK to compute token counts before sending (see ignite-integration-notes.md).

4) Streaming + tool calling: during streaming the SDK emits partial tokens as they arrive. If the model decides to emit a structured tool call (function call JSON), the SDK will emit a special event when the call payload is complete — the stream is paused while the runtime executes the tool call (if configured server-side), then resumes with the tool result appended. In other words: partial token events continue until a tool-call boundary; tool-call payloads are emitted atomically. This ensures your UI can show partial text but still handle actions deterministically.

Attachments included:
- ignite-integration-notes.md: auth exchange examples, routing policy pseudocode, preferred schema for tool-calls, tokenizer probe usage.
- redwood-auth-snippet.py: Python example to mint short-lived scoped tokens.

Proposed next steps:
- Tech sync (30m) — please propose windows Thu/Fri morning PT.
- We’ll deliver a PoC checklist and a small evaluation dataset template (50 representative queries) for you to run through the reranker.

If helpful I can also include a minimal Node SDK snippet that shows streaming + tool-call handling.

Thanks,
Ben
